summary: Quick hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics. Covered streaming responses, key parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop), retries and idempotency, SDK examples, and using Redwood Console to pick models and monitor tokens. Customer concerned about latency and data residency; asked about security (SOC2, KMS) and retry behavior for partial streams. Agreed to share security pack and trial API keys and run a short latency benchmark with customer's sample prompts.
topics: Introductions; customer goals and constraints; hosted API capabilities; streaming demo; params and examples; retries and idempotency; console walkthrough (model selection, rate limits); questions about privacy/compliance; next steps and action items
transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through Redwood's hosted API, chat and text generation basics. I'm Liam, AE on the account. Sofia and Priya from SE team are here too.
[00:12] Dana Brooks: Hi Liam, thanks \u0014 quick intro, I'm Dana, CTO at Nimbus Health \u0014 we're exploring adding clinical note summarization and triage chat responses, low latency is pretty important.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, ML eng, we'll want to test throughput on typical batch sizes and see token costs.
[00:28] Liam Chen: Great, that's the right framing. Quick agenda: demo streaming, parameters, retries/backoff and then the Redwood Console and Optimize hints.
[00:45] Sofia Martinez: I'll kick off with a quick streaming demo \u0014 show how the response streams back via the SDK and the HTTP SSE stream. Note: live transcription might write 'S S E', sometimes it's 'S-S-E' in logs.
[01:05] Sofia Martinez: (shares screen) Here's a simple chat call, messages array, model param set to one of our recommended open models, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9, max_tokens 256. I'm toggling stream=true. You'll see chunked responses arriving every 150-400ms depending on the model and region.
[01:28] Marcus Lee: How do you handle partial tokens if the connection drops?
[01:34] Priya Rao: Good question \u0014 we recommend an idempotency token on the request so retries don't double charge, and the client can replay or resume depending on your implementation. For streaming specifically, we surface complete chunks and a final 'done' event; if a connection is interrupted mid-stream, a retry will generate a fresh response unless you persist the prefix locally. We also offer continuations via conversation state if you want deterministic resumptions.
[02:02] Dana Brooks: Hmm, continuations as in server-side KV cache?
[02:07] Sofia Martinez: Exactly, we have prefix/KV cache support in our runtime; sometimes transcribed as 'K V cache' in notes. That cache reduces token egress for repeated prefixes which helps with cost and latency.
[02:20] Liam Chen: When we talk about retries we also mean exponential backoff for 5xx errors and idempotency for 429s if safe. Our SDK has built-in retry middleware but you can configure it \u0014 e.g., maxRetries: 3, backoffFactor: 2, jitter: true.
[02:40] Marcus Lee: Are retries surfaced as events or do we just see final success/fail?
[02:45] Priya Rao: The SDK emits hooks \u0014 request start, retry, final, so you can log each. The hosted API itself will surface error codes and a request_id for tracing.
[03:05] Aisha Khan: On data residency \u0014 we need EU data to stay in EU. Can hosted do region pinning?
[03:10] Sofia Martinez: Yes, you can route to region-specific endpoints; we also offer VPC/private options for Private deployments but hosted supports region selection for inference zones.
[03:22] Liam Chen: Demo note: watch the console for token-level cost and latency breakdown on the right \u0014 I'm switching to the Console.
[03:30] (screen) \"Redwood Console\" shows model catalog, streaming toggle, retry settings.
[03:40] Sofia Martinez: Here's model selection \u0014 we surface performance profiles and recommended params. For chat, start low temp like 0.0-0.2 for deterministic clinical summaries; for creative tasks raise to 0.7+.
[03:58] Marcus Lee: What about safety filters and redactions for PHI?
[04:03] Priya Rao: We have content filters and enterprise redaction hooks; for regulated data, customers commonly use our Private option with KMS and audit logs. We'll send the security packet.
[04:15] Dana Brooks: Can you demonstrate a streaming chat example that includes function/tool calls?
[04:20] Sofia Martinez: Sure, quick example \u0014 chat messages include a tool call intent; the server streams a partial response, then emits a tool request, then resumes with the tool output. You'll see the sequence: model chunk, tool_call event, tool result, final chunk.
[04:48] (audio overlap) Liam Chen: Sorry slight crosstalk \u0014 Marcus asked about token accounting during streaming, yes each chunk counts toward token usage when emitted.
[05:03] Marcus Lee: Any way to reduce token costs for repeated prompts?
[05:06] Sofia Martinez: As mentioned, prefix caching and prompt templating helps \u0014 Redwood Optimize offers recommendations: quantization, batching policy, and which model variant gives best cost/latency for your workload. In Console we show per-route token usage and suggest models. Sometimes notes show 'Optimize' as 'Optima' in the transcript.
[05:25] Dana Brooks: For latency SLOs, what's realistic for a 512-token response?
[05:31] Priya Rao: On dedicated capacity you can get single-digit token latency, hosted depends on model and region. For example, our curated 7B-like variant in us-west typical round-trip for 512 tokens is ~600-1200ms in optimistic conditions; larger models can be multiple seconds. We'll run benchmarks with your prompts to give concrete numbers.
[06:01] Marcus Lee: Does the SDK support streaming over websockets or just SSE/HTTP2?
[06:06] Sofia Martinez: We support SSE, HTTP/2 streaming, and a websocket client in the SDK. Implementation detail sometimes garbles as 'web-socket' in notes.
[06:20] Liam Chen: Walkthrough of params \u0014 temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, presence/penalty. Also importance of system messages for instruction steering.
[06:35] Sofia Martinez: Quick live edit: set temperature 0.0 and stop ['\n\n'] for a hard stop on multi-paragraph clinical output. You can also use token_limit hints to prevent long tails.
[06:55] Dana Brooks: About rate limits \u0014 we expect bursty traffic during morning triage. Can hosted support bursts?
[07:02] Priya Rao: Hosted has rate limits and quotas; we offer burst capacity options and for predictability Dedicated reserved capacity is recommended. You can also configure autoscale rules for Dedicated.
[07:20] Marcus Lee: How do you do canary rollouts if we update a system prompt or model?
[07:25] Sofia Martinez: Console supports route-level rollout policies \u0014 canary, percent-based, or A/B. Also automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency spikes.
[07:40] Liam Chen: I'm going to show a short code snippet of the SDK streaming in Node. (reads code) const stream = client.chat.stream({model: 'redwood-7b-curated', messages, stream: true, temperature: 0.1}); stream.on('data', chunk => append(chunk)); stream.on('done', () => console.log('complete'));
[08:05] Marcus Lee: For billing \u0014 if a stream fails mid-response and we retry, are we billed twice?
[08:10] Priya Rao: We bill tokens emitted by the model. If the stream produced N tokens before a failure, those count. A retry produces a new response billed separately unless you use our prefix cache reductions or dedupe via idempotency and replay locally. We can work with you on minimizing retried output for sensitive workloads.
[08:30] Dana Brooks: Anything about encryption at rest and KMS?
[08:34] Sofia Martinez: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private; for hosted we use encrypted storage and rotate keys regularly \u0014 details in the security whitepaper.
[08:50] (timestamp jump) [15:12] Sofia Martinez: Now running through a small demo that simulates a dropped connection and shows the SDK handling a retry with exponential backoff. You'll hear log entries: 'retrying request id r-1234, attempt 2'.
[15:34] Marcus Lee: In that demo, did the SDK preserve the conversation id?
[15:38] Priya Rao: Yes, conversation id persists server-side and the SDK includes conversation_id if provided \u0014 but note server-side resumptions depend on cache window and TTL.
[16:05] Dana Brooks: We need audit logs for every API call for compliance \u0014 is that available?
[16:12] Sofia Martinez: Yes, hosted has audit logs with request_id, timestamp, user, and model used. For enterprise we can increase retention and push logs to your SIEM.
[16:30] Marcus Lee: Performance question \u0014 you said batching reduces per-token cost; how aggressive is batching without hurting latency?
[16:38] Priya Rao: The runtime does continuous batching and you can set latency SLOs; it's workload dependent. For tight latency we reduce batch collect window and favor immediate dispatch. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions based on observed request distribution.
[16:58] Aisha Khan: Is there an examples repo for integration?
[17:02] Liam Chen: Yes \u0014 we'll share a GitHub repo with sample notebook showing streaming, retries, and console links.
[17:12] (short silence)
[17:20] Liam Chen: Any remaining security/budget concerns?
[17:23] Dana Brooks: Budget \u0014 need cost per 1M tokens estimate for the recommended model.
[17:27] Liam Chen: We'll include that in the pricing note \u0014 rough hosted number and then reserved capacity options for Dedicated.
[17:40] Marcus Lee: Could you run a micro-benchmark for 100 concurrent short chats \u0014 to see p95 latency?
[17:45] Priya Rao: Absolutely, if you share prompt set and desired concurrency we'll run it on hosted and/or Dedicated dev cluster and report back.
[18:00] (screen) Sofia Martinez: Quick Console tip \u0014 you can set per-route model, per-route rate limiting, and view invocation traces.
[18:12] Marcus Lee: Any pitfalls to watch for implementing streaming in frontend?
[18:18] Priya Rao: Ensure your client handles partial chunks, content-lengthless responses and reassembles. Use idempotency to avoid duplicates. Also consider backpressure on the UI if chunks are large.
[18:40] Dana Brooks: Are there compliance customers in healthcare using hosted?
[18:43] Sofia Martinez: Some healthcare customers use hosted with strict controls, many move to Private for PHI-heavy workloads. We'll include references.
[19:00] (fast forward) [28:05] Liam Chen: Wrapping up \u0014 main ask is we send security docs, pricing, and trial keys. Also schedule benchmarks.
[28:20] Dana Brooks: That works. One more question \u0014 can we set policy-based routing by customer tenancy?
[28:25] Priya Rao: Yes, smart routing supports policy rules: latency-first, cost-first, or region-first; you can pin to a model variant per customer.
[28:40] (closing) [33:10] Liam Chen: Thanks everyone \u0014 we'll follow up with the packet.
[33:18] Marcus Lee: Thanks.
[33:20] Dana Brooks: Thanks, talk soon.
[33:25] (meeting ends, recording stops)
closing_notes: Customer aligned on next steps: pricing, security docs, trial keys, and benchmark. Action items assigned. Agreed to run a 100-concurrent short-chat benchmark once Nimbus provides prompts. Follow-ups scheduled via AE.
